summary: Redstone torches on repeaters and comparators are shaded differently from normal redstone torches
description:
The resource pack attached to 
 
 
 
 MC-214686
 
 Resolved
 
 offers a complete fix for this issue. Mojang have my full permission to (and are encouraged to) replace the affected vanilla model files with the contents of the resource pack.

## The bug

The torches on redstone repeaters and redstone comparators appear darker than expected, and are shaded depending on the view direction. This is not the case with redstone torches themselves, which are fully lit regardless of the view direction.

This began in 1.8, and was not the case in 1.7 or earlier. In addition, this is not the case in Bedrock Edition, effectively also making this a parity issue.

While this was listed in 
 
 
 
 MC-68302
 
 Resolved
 
, I still strongly consider this behaviour unintended for many reasons, including the two stated above. In addition, MC-67830's resolution contradicts such an assertion of this being intended. Other reasons are listed in 
 
 
 
 MC-236474
 
 Reopened
 
, a very similar issue.

## How to reproduce

 - Place down a redstone torch, noting how bright it appears when in the "on" state

 - Place down a redstone repeater in a way that the torch powers it

 - Note that the torches on said redstone repeater are darker than the standalone torch

 - Now place down a comparator which also receives power

 - Note that it, too, has darker torches than one would expect

## Expected behaviour

The torches on repeaters and comparators would appear as bright as redstone torches themselves

## Actual behaviour

Repeater and comparator torches are noticeably darker

## How to fix

The resource pack attached to 
 
 
 
 MC-214686
 
 Resolved
 
 fixes this issue completely.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a Creative world with default settings.
3. Place a redstone torch.
4. Observe the brightness of the redstone torch while it is on.
5. Place a redstone repeater so that the redstone torch powers it.
6. Observe that the repeater’s torches appear darker than the standalone redstone torch.
7. Place a redstone comparator so that it receives power.
8. Observe that the comparator’s torches also appear darker than the standalone redstone torch and that their shading changes depending on the viewing direction.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.5, 21w05b, 21w06a, 21w07a, 21w08b, 21w13a, 21w17a, 21w20a, 1.17 Pre-release 1, 1.17, 1.17.1 Pre-release 1, 1.17.1, 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w42a, 1.18 Pre-release 1, 1.18, 1.18.1 Pre-release 1, 1.18.1, 22w06a, 1.18.2, 22w11a, 1.19 Pre-release 1, 1.19, 1.19.1 Pre-release 3, 1.19.4, 23w14a, 1.20.1, 1.20.4, 1.21 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior:
## Actual behaviour

When powered, the two redstone torches modeled on a redstone repeater and the three torches modeled on a redstone comparator are rendered visibly darker than a standalone lit redstone torch. Their brightness also changes with the camera’s viewing direction, causing different sides of the torch models to appear shaded.

This is a visual rendering issue only: the repeater and comparator remain powered and function normally. The standalone redstone torch does not exhibit the same directional shading and remains consistently bright when lit.
Expected Behavior: When powered, the torches on redstone repeaters and redstone comparators should appear equally bright as standalone redstone torches. Their brightness should remain consistent regardless of the viewing direction, without darker shading or directional lighting differences. This behavior should be consistent for both repeater and comparator torches when compared with normal, fully lit redstone torches.
